correctness.rationale: The substitution identities force distinct starting parities to give different factors at length at least four; same-parity factors are injective encodings of source factors of lengths \(m\) or \(m+1\). These establish \(I(n)=2I(\lfloor n/2\rfloor)\), with exact lifting of the unique previous collision position. The three base cases then imply the claimed all-length formula. Independently generated prefixes and literal first-collision checks agree for \(1\le n\le1024\); finite tests are corroboration only.

value.rationale: Initial non-repetitive complexity is a natural established invariant for identifying how long a sequence supplies fresh local information. The finding closes a missing classical substitution example at all positive lengths, gives exact collisions not merely bounds, and proves a sharp two-regime dyadic law with normalized lower and upper accumulation values. This is a motivated complete classification rather than a finite or arbitrary parameter slice.
